title: Regional cells: the fold, first occurrence, region counts and cell trees
generator: Printed by packages/crypto/scripts/regional-cells-vectors.py, written from docs/spec/election-definition.md (Layout (version 3), Regional cells, Well-formedness) and docs/spec/membership.md (Cell tree) with only the Python standard library, independently of packages/crypto, reusing definition-vectors.py's encoders and tier-tree-vectors.py's self-checked Poseidon2 and tier tree. Its own implementation of the rules confirms every valid vector's illFormed label (or its absence); decode errors are labelled by hand.

folds.note: one region is one cell, however small
one region above the floor is still one cell
every region at or above the floor: one cell each, no remainder
two large regions and small ones summing to exactly the floor
small regions summing to 999: the tier isn't split
one large region and a remainder at the floor: two cells
only small regions, summing past the floor: one candidate cell, so not split
999 and 1000: the 999 alone is a remainder below the floor, so not split
the remainder is last whatever the region order
a remainder below the floor is never rescued by merging a large region

tiers.note: one region of one group: the cell tree is that group's tier tree
a commitment in two groups of one region counts once, in the lower group_id
a commitment added twice to one group counts once: its second leaf is 0
a commitment removed from a lower group counts in the higher one; removed and forbidden leaves are 0
a cell's leaves follow ascending group_id, not region order
two large regions (one of two groups) and a remainder of two small ones: three cells
the victim's commitment, also added to a lower group in another region, counts there: its own leaf is 0
1000 additions with one repeat count 999, so the region is small and folds; the remainder is below the floor, so the tier isn't split
